chunks: From him, from Abu al-Mu'za, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gives a gift exclusively to one of his children. He said: 'If he is wealthy, yes; and if he is poor, no.'

key_terms.النُّحْلِ: Exclusive gift given to one child

ai.seo_question: Can a father give a gift to only one of his children according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction in *al-nuhla* (exclusive gifting) based on the father's financial capacity. While a wealthy father may favor one child without creating an obligation of equalization (*i'tidal*) upon death, a poor father is advised against it to prevent perceived inequity among his offspring. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining familial harmony and preventing jealousy, grounded in the principle that gifts from the less affluent are more scrutinized for fairness.
